posts.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
posts.description: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

posts.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
posts.description: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. posts.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
posts.description: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.
